findings.claim: Propagate compound patch validation to renderer stream handlers. The new getByPath/setByPath rejection outcomes are not handled by the older renderer applyPatch implementations. Built React useUIStream processing move from /state/source to /state/items/01 removes source then silently rejects its destination. Copy/move from /state/items/01 to a valid key creates an own undefined property. Core applySpecStreamPatch safely rejects the same compound patches, but these handlers bypass it. This introduces data loss when noncanonical input previously coerced to index 1.

findings.claim: Exclude rejected batch entries from state-provider change callbacks. After update({"/items/01":"rejected","/count":1}), new core state correctly preserves items but StateProvider onStateChange reports both entries because it compares submitted values with the old snapshot. Applications persisting callbacks receive a write that never occurred. Exact base executed the coerced array write, so the same callback matched its state; the new rejection exposes this mismatch.
